sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Greek mythology is filled with stories of violence, anger, and hatred.
sentences.zh: 希腊神话中充满了暴力、愤怒和仇恨的故事。

sentences.en: Take the tale of the goddess Medea.
sentences.zh: 以美狄亚女神的传说为例。

sentences.en: To distract her father as she fled with her lover,
sentences.zh: 为了在与情人私奔时分散父亲的注意力，

sentences.en: Medea killed her brother, cut up his body, and scattered the pieces behind her.
sentences.zh: 美狄亚杀死了自己的弟弟，将他的尸体切碎，并把碎片散落在身后。

sentences.en: Then there's the god Kronos, who devoured five of his children at birth
sentences.zh: 还有克洛诺斯神，他在孩子出生时就吞食了五个孩子，

sentences.en: to ward off a prophecy that one of them would eventually overthrow him.
sentences.zh: 以阻止一个预言，即其中一个孩子最终会推翻他。

sentences.en: For a land blessed with exceptional sunshine and good wine,
sentences.zh: 对于一个拥有充足阳光和美酒的土地来说，

sentences.en: Greece is home to a striking number of tales about incest,
sentences.zh: 希腊却有着惊人数量关于乱伦、

sentences.en: brutality, and bloodthirsty revenge.
sentences.zh: 残暴和嗜血复仇的故事。

sentences.en: Thousands of years ago, the Greek philosopher Aristotle
sentences.zh: 几千年前，希腊哲学家亚里士多德

sentences.en: had a theory of why this was.
sentences.zh: 曾提出过一个关于为何如此的理论。

sentences.en: In Poetics, he suggested that the goal of art
sentences.zh: 在《诗学》中，他提出艺术的目标

sentences.en: was something he called catharsis.
sentences.zh: 是他所称的“宣泄”。

sentences.en: The idea that stories can be a form of therapy has carried over into modern times.
sentences.zh: 故事可以作为一种治疗形式的观点一直延续到了现代。

sentences.en: Sigmund Freud explored the idea.
sentences.zh: 西格蒙德·弗洛伊德探索过这个想法。

sentences.en: Psychoanalysis involves understanding the self as a series of stories.
sentences.zh: 精神分析涉及将自我理解为一系列故事。

sentences.en: After Freud fell out of favor, researchers and counselors have continued to explore the role
sentences.zh: 在弗洛伊德不再受宠后，研究人员和咨询师们继续探索

sentences.en: that stories play in our mental well-being.
sentences.zh: 故事在我们心理健康中所扮演的角色。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain,
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，

sentences.en: how understanding the stories of our lives
sentences.zh: 了解我们生命中的故事

sentences.en: and rewriting them can change us forever.
sentences.zh: 并重写它们将如何永远改变我们。

sentences.en: A quick heads up,
sentences.zh: 温馨提示，

sentences.en: today's episode touches on trauma
sentences.zh: 今天的节目涉及创伤

sentences.en: and how we cope with it.
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何应对它。

sentences.en: There are references to suicide and revenge.
sentences.zh: 其中提到了自杀和复仇。

sentences.en: Rachel first met Greg in California.
sentences.zh: 瑞秋最初是在加利福尼亚遇到格雷格的。

sentences.en: They were skydiving.
sentences.zh: 他们当时在跳伞。

sentences.en: They were at what's known as the drop zone
sentences.zh: 他们在所谓的降落区，

sentences.en: where skydivers gather after a jump.
sentences.zh: 那是跳伞者跳伞后聚集的地方。

sentences.en: He was funny.
sentences.zh: 他很风趣。

sentences.en: He was kind.
sentences.zh: 他很善良。

sentences.en: He was intelligent.
sentences.zh: 他很聪明。

sentences.en: He was also good-looking.
sentences.zh: 他还长得很帅。

sentences.en: We are using first names to protect the privacy of people in the story.
sentences.zh: 为了保护故事中人物的隐私，我们使用了名字。

sentences.en: He has beautiful eyes, kind face, wonderful sense of humor.
sentences.zh: 他有一双美丽的眼睛，和善的面孔，还有极好的幽默感。

sentences.en: Skydivers tend to be a lot of A-type personalities, a lot of ego, but he wasn't like that.
sentences.zh: 跳伞者往往有很多A型人格，自尊心很强，但他不是那样的人。

sentences.en: He didn't have this need to be the center of attention.
sentences.zh: 他没有那种成为关注焦点的需求。

sentences.en: I found that appealing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这一点很吸引人。

sentences.en: Rachel started to see more of Greg.
sentences.zh: 瑞秋开始更多地见到格雷格。

sentences.en: And she noticed that he made a point of putting himself on the same jumps she was on.
sentences.zh: 她注意到他特意让自己参加和她一样的跳伞活动。

sentences.en: So one day...
sentences.zh: 所以有一天……

sentences.en: He was sitting on the grass having lunch.
sentences.zh: 他正坐在草地上吃午饭。

sentences.en: I came over with an extra Mountain Dew or some kind of soda.
sentences.zh: 我带着多余的激浪汽水或其他什么饮料走过去。

sentences.en: And we sat down and just started making small talk.
sentences.zh: 我们坐下来，开始闲聊。

sentences.en: Shortly after that first chat, they started dating.
sentences.zh: 在那次初次交谈后不久，他们就开始约会了。

sentences.en: Three months in, Rachel was doing a jump during some rough weather.
sentences.zh: 三个月后，瑞秋在天气恶劣的情况下进行了一次跳伞。

sentences.en: And I came in on some very windy conditions and had a little accident and nothing major, but I did break my wriSt.
sentences.zh: 我在大风条件下着陆时出了点小事故，没什么大碍，但确实摔断了手腕。

sentences.en: Greg offered to come over and take care of her while she healed.
sentences.zh: 格雷格主动提出过来照顾她，直到她康复。

sentences.en: We spent a lot of time together at that point, and I was tickled and delighted.
sentences.zh: 那时我们花了很多时间在一起，我感到非常开心和愉悦。

sentences.en: Greg never moved out, and soon they were engaged.
sentences.zh: 格雷格再也没有搬走，不久他们就订婚了。

sentences.en: About a year later, Rachel and Greg went skydiving in Arizona.
sentences.zh: 大约一年后，瑞秋和格雷格去亚利桑那州跳伞。

sentences.en: She recorded some of the jumps on her GoPro.
sentences.zh: 她用GoPro记录了一些跳伞过程。

sentences.en: It was still very early in the morning.
sentences.zh: 当时还是清晨。

sentences.en: It's an amazing experience.
sentences.zh: 那是一种奇妙的体验。

sentences.en: You have about a minute of free fall, and then you break away, and then you deploy your canopies.
sentences.zh: 你有大约一分钟的自由落体时间，然后脱离，接着打开降落伞。

sentences.en: After landing, they quickly went up again.
sentences.zh: 着陆后，他们很快又上去了。

sentences.en: Thousands of feet above the Arizona desert, they jumped.
sentences.zh: 在亚利桑那沙漠上空几千英尺处，他们跳了下去。

sentences.en: We did another free fly jump with two other people.
sentences.zh: 我们和另外两个人又做了一次自由飞行跳伞。

sentences.en: We did what's called a four-way.
sentences.zh: 我们做了所谓的“四人编队”。

sentences.en: You have to come in in a certain pattern, you have to pick your spot, and you do a landing pattern.
sentences.zh: 你必须以特定的模式进入，必须选好你的位置，然后按照着陆模式进行。

sentences.en: When they broke away for the landing, Greg went firSt.
sentences.zh: 当他们脱离准备着陆时，格雷格先走了。

sentences.en: As he neared the ground, Rachel noticed something that looked like a little tornado below her.
sentences.zh: 当他接近地面时，瑞秋注意到他下方出现了一个看起来像小龙卷风的东西。

sentences.en: The weather, as it warms up, can create dust devils.
sentences.zh: 天气变暖时，会产生尘卷风。

sentences.en: Greg was headed straight into one.
sentences.zh: 格雷格正径直冲向其中一个。

sentences.en: Just before she made her own landing, Rachel caught one last glimpse of him.
sentences.zh: 就在她自己着陆前，瑞秋最后看了一眼他。

sentences.en: I can see him completely splayed on the ground.
sentences.zh: 我看到他整个人瘫在地上。

sentences.en: I can see his canopy is completely collapsed.
sentences.zh: 我看到他的降落伞完全坍塌了。

sentences.en: It shouldn't have been collapsed at that point.
sentences.zh: 在那个时候它本不该坍塌的。

sentences.en: I can see people running toward him.
sentences.zh: 我看到人们向他跑去。

sentences.en: Rachel landed safely and rushed to Greg.
sentences.zh: 瑞秋安全着陆并冲向格雷格。

sentences.en: His face is contorted in pain.
sentences.zh: 他的脸因痛苦而扭曲。

sentences.en: They've just pulled off his shoe.
sentences.zh: 他们刚刚脱掉了他的鞋子。

sentences.en: He has a bone sticking out of his foot.
sentences.zh: 他的脚上有一根骨头露了出来。

sentences.en: He has a busted femur.
sentences.zh: 他的股骨骨折了。

sentences.en: Both feet are broken.
sentences.zh: 双脚都骨折了。

sentences.en: Greg was medevaced to a trauma center.
sentences.zh: 格雷格被医疗直升机送往创伤中心。

sentences.en: Rachel followed by Carr.
sentences.zh: 瑞秋开车跟在后面。

sentences.en: He was already in surgery when she got there.
sentences.zh: 她赶到时，他已经在手术中了。

sentences.en: His first surgery to repair his femur, they put a rod down his leg.
sentences.zh: 他修复股骨的第一次手术，医生在他的腿里植入了一根钢钉。

sentences.en: It turns out that the initial injury, which was the femur fracture, was the easiest to fix.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，最初的损伤，也就是股骨骨折，是最容易修复的。

sentences.en: It turns out that his feet and his leg and his lumbar area would all just have issues.
sentences.zh: 结果他的脚、腿和腰部都出现了问题。

sentences.en: Greg was sent home to continue his healing.
sentences.zh: 格雷格被送回家继续康复。

sentences.en: A primary care physician took over his case.
sentences.zh: 一位初级保健医生接手了他的病例。

sentences.en: She was new, a replacement for Greg's longtime doctor, who'd recently retired.
sentences.zh: 她是新来的，接替了格雷格刚退休的长期医生。

sentences.en: Greg's biggest issue now was pain.
sentences.zh: 格雷格现在最大的问题是疼痛。

sentences.en: It was almost unbearable.
sentences.zh: 几乎难以忍受。

sentences.en: Still, they felt sure that with time and good medical care, it would ease.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他们仍觉得只要有时间和良好的医疗护理，疼痛就会减轻。

sentences.en: We felt like we were beating the odds.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得我们正在战胜困难。

sentences.en: He kept his feet, and it was just, it was hard, but we were going to get through it.
sentences.zh: 他保住了双脚，这只是……虽然很难，但我们能挺过去。

sentences.en: But Rachel says the new doctor was cautious.
sentences.zh: 但瑞秋说这位新医生很谨慎。

sentences.en: Doctors who treat pain have to balance competing goals.
sentences.zh: 治疗疼痛的医生必须平衡相互竞争的目标。

sentences.en: They want to minimize pain as much as possible,
sentences.zh: 他们想尽可能地减轻疼痛，

sentences.en: but as the recent opioid epidemic shows,
sentences.zh: 但正如最近的阿片类药物流行所显示的那样，

sentences.en: the strongest drugs can also harm patients and lead to deadly addictions.
sentences.zh: 最强效的药物也可能伤害患者并导致致命的成瘾。

sentences.en: How far do you go with medications?
sentences.zh: 药物治疗要到什么程度？

sentences.en: How fast?
sentences.zh: 多快？

sentences.en: These are tough questions that often do not have clear-cut answers.
sentences.zh: 这些都是棘手的问题，往往没有明确的答案。

sentences.en: She had a protocol.
sentences.zh: 她有一套方案。

sentences.en: I remember her showing it to me once,
sentences.zh: 我记得她曾给我看过一次，

sentences.en: and she was going to try each drug.
sentences.zh: 她打算尝试每一种药物。

sentences.en: Well, each drug has to be approved.
sentences.zh: 嗯，每种药物都必须经过批准。

sentences.en: He has to try it for a few weeks.
sentences.zh: 他必须试用几周。

sentences.en: If it doesn't work, we have to come in.
sentences.zh: 如果不起作用，我们就得去复诊。

sentences.en: We have to look at the next one.
sentences.zh: 我们得考虑下一种。

sentences.en: Nothing eased Greg's pain.
sentences.zh: 没有任何东西能缓解格雷格的疼痛。

sentences.en: He told me on a regular basis it was like someone was stabbing him with a knife and turning the knife.
sentences.zh: 他经常告诉我，那种感觉就像有人用刀捅他，还在转动刀子。

sentences.en: And he just was constant.
sentences.zh: 而且那种感觉一直持续着。

sentences.en: This is the kind of pain, you know, it's a nightmare.
sentences.zh: 这种疼痛，你知道，简直是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: Rachel felt powerless.
sentences.zh: 瑞秋感到无能为力。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Greg got worse and worse.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，格雷格的情况越来越糟。

sentences.en: He stopped getting out of bed.
sentences.zh: 他不再下床了。

sentences.en: He was gradually not eating.
sentences.zh: 他逐渐不再进食。

sentences.en: He was curling up in a ball.
sentences.zh: 他蜷缩成一团。

sentences.en: He was just shutting down,
sentences.zh: 他只是在自我封闭，

sentences.en: and he would tell me about how much pain he was in,
sentences.zh: 他会告诉我他有多痛苦，

sentences.en: and then he wouldn't talk for the rest of the day.
sentences.zh: 然后那天剩下的时间里他就不再说话了。

sentences.en: Rachel says Greg told her he couldn't endure the pain
sentences.zh: 瑞秋说格雷格告诉她，他无法忍受这种痛苦，

sentences.en: and that he began to talk about killing himself.
sentences.zh: 并开始谈论自杀。

sentences.en: He says, I feel like I'm scratching my fingernails on rocks
sentences.zh: 他说，我觉得自己就像在岩石上抓挠指甲，

sentences.en: trying to pull myself out of a well,
sentences.zh: 试图把自己从井里拉出来，

sentences.en: and I just keep sinking further and further in,
sentences.zh: 但我却不断地越陷越深，

sentences.en: and I want to end it.
sentences.zh: 我想结束这一切。

sentences.en: Rachel found a pilot who agreed to fly Greg to a hospital in Mexico.
sentences.zh: 瑞秋找到了一名飞行员，同意将格雷格飞往墨西哥的一家医院。

sentences.en: He could receive stronger pain medication there.
sentences.zh: 他在那里可以接受更强效的止痛药。

sentences.en: But Rachel says that doctors said it would take a few weeks
sentences.zh: 但瑞秋说医生们表示，转移他的医疗记录需要几周时间。

sentences.en: to transfer his medical records.
sentences.zh: 我说，我们没有几周的时间了。

sentences.en: And I said, we don't have a few weeks.
sentences.zh: 这是紧急情况。

sentences.en: This is an emergency.
sentences.zh: 他撑不过去了。

sentences.en: He's not going to make it.
sentences.zh: 他的状况太糟糕了。

sentences.en: He is in such terrible condition.
sentences.zh: 再一次，就像是对牛弹琴。

sentences.en: And again, it was like talking to a brick wall.
sentences.zh: 当医生转身离开时，瑞秋记得自己做了一件意想不到的事。

sentences.en: As the doctor turned to leave, Rachel remembers doing something unexpected.
sentences.zh: 她跪了下来。

sentences.en: She fell to her knees.
sentences.zh: 我看着她，又看着她的员工。

sentences.en: And I looked at her and I looked at her staff.
sentences.zh: 房间里还有另外几名女性。

sentences.en: There was a couple other women in the room.
sentences.zh: 我说，求求你们，这非常重要。

sentences.en: And I said, please, this is so important.
sentences.zh: 他撑不过去了。

sentences.en: He's not going to make it.
sentences.zh: 他太痛苦了。

sentences.en: He's in so much pain.
sentences.zh: 求求你们，我恳求你们，救救他。

sentences.en: Please, I'm begging you, help him.
sentences.zh: 她们只是看着我。

sentences.en: And they just looked at me.
sentences.zh: 那几个女孩看起来很难过。

sentences.en: The couple of other gals, they looked upset.
sentences.zh: 但她们什么也没说，她只是看着我说，

sentences.en: But they didn't say anything, and she just looked at me and she says,
sentences.zh: 我们必须等待这个方案起效。

sentences.en: we have to wait for this to work.
sentences.zh: 然后她转过身离开了。

sentences.en: And she turned around and she left.
sentences.zh: 五天后，格雷格把自己拖进了一辆车里。

sentences.en: Five days later, Greg hauled himself into a car.
sentences.zh: 他爬上了一栋高楼的顶端，

sentences.en: He got himself to the top of a tall building,
sentences.zh: 然后从边缘跳了下去。

sentences.en: and he flung himself over the edge.
sentences.zh: 他在跳下去之前拨打了911。

sentences.en: He called 911 right before he did it,
sentences.zh: 他拨打了911。

sentences.en: so that he wouldn't be laying there, he didn't want to upset anybody.
sentences.zh: 为了不让他躺在那里，他不想让任何人难过。

sentences.en: He left a note at the house.
sentences.zh: 他在屋里留了一张字条。

sentences.en: It was a scrawl in this crazy handwriting.
sentences.zh: 那是一行潦草的、疯狂的笔迹。

sentences.en: It was basically, I don't want to die.
sentences.zh: 内容基本上是，我不想死。

sentences.en: I'm so sorry to go.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉要走了。

sentences.en: I love you, but I just can't take it anymore.
sentences.zh: 我爱你，但我真的受不了了。

sentences.en: The first call Rachel made was to the doctor.
sentences.zh: 瑞秋打的第一个电话是给医生的。

sentences.en: I got her on the phone, and I told her,
sentences.zh: 我接通了她的电话，然后告诉她，

sentences.en: I said, you know, he killed himself.
sentences.zh: 我说，你知道，他自杀了。

sentences.en: This is your fault.
sentences.zh: 这是你的错。

sentences.en: Rachel can't remember how the doctor replied,
sentences.zh: 瑞秋记不清医生是怎么回答的了，

sentences.en: but she says it wasn't what she needed to hear.
sentences.zh: 但她说那并不是她想听到的。

sentences.en: I was so upset with her.
sentences.zh: 我对她感到非常难过。

sentences.en: I kept feeling like this didn't have to go this way.
sentences.zh: 我一直觉得事情本不必如此。

sentences.en: You could have helped him.
sentences.zh: 你本可以帮帮他的。

sentences.en: We could have, you know, maybe lost his feet or something,
sentences.zh: 我们本可以，你知道，也许失去他的双脚什么的，

sentences.en: but he could have been here,
sentences.zh: 但他本可以留在这里，

sentences.en: and he certainly could have been kept comfortable.
sentences.zh: 而且他当然可以得到妥善的照顾。

sentences.en: I mean, nobody treats a person like this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没有人会这样对待一个人。

sentences.en: We don't treat animals like this.
sentences.zh: 我们连对待动物都不会这样。

sentences.en: We do not know the name of Greg's doctor,
sentences.zh: 我们不知道格雷医生的名字，

sentences.en: and our story is not about whether she did something wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们的故事也不是关于她是否做错了什么。

sentences.en: Our story is about how Rachel saw things
sentences.zh: 我们的故事是关于瑞秋如何看待这些事情，

sentences.en: and what happened next in her mind.
sentences.zh: 以及她脑海中接下来发生了什么。

sentences.en: As the days passed, Rachel's grief turned to rage.
sentences.zh: 随着日子一天天过去，瑞秋的悲伤变成了愤怒。

sentences.en: She began fantasizing about revenge.
sentences.zh: 她开始幻想复仇。

sentences.en: Rachel knew she and the doctor lived in the same town.
sentences.zh: 瑞秋知道她和那位医生住在同一个镇上。

sentences.en: She kept thinking about what would happen
sentences.zh: 她一直在想，如果她在商店里碰见她，

sentences.en: if she bumped into her at the store.
sentences.zh: 会发生什么。

sentences.en: I imagined that I would see her in an aisle, and I would walk up to her, and she'd see me,
sentences.zh: 我幻想在过道里看到她，我会走过去，她会看到我，

sentences.en: and I'd see her, and I'd spit in her face.

sentences.en: And the more involved it got, the more it occurred to me that, well, if I follow through,

sentences.en: Rachel eventually confided her fantasy to a grief counselor.
sentences.zh: 瑞秋最终向一位悲伤咨询师吐露了她的幻想。

sentences.en: And she jumped on it.
sentences.zh: 她立刻抓住了重点。

sentences.en: And she basically said, you need to stop thinking about that right now.
sentences.zh: 她基本上说，你现在必须停止考虑这件事。

sentences.en: You've got this way too planned out.

sentences.en: Do you know what will happen if you do that?

sentences.zh: 你会

sentences.en: And I remember being shocked, and I remember thinking it was
sentences.zh: 我记得当时很震惊，我记得我当时想，

sentences.en: And once the therapist asked you to let this go,

sentences.en: I did a lot of journaling, and I realized that I had been caught up in some kind of,

sentences.en: I realized that if a counselor hadn't talked to me,

sentences.en: I think I had the potential to act on it.

sentences.en: The fantasy just kept getting richer and richer.

sentences.en: As each, you know, few days would go by, and I ultimately decided that for the rest of my life, if I think she's anywhere nearby, I will leave.

sentences.en: Was Rachel's fantasy of revenge a precursor to her committing a crime?

sentences.en: Her grief counselor worried about that.

sentences.en: Rachel worried about that, too.

sentences.en: Such a response is understandable.

sentences.en: But it also reflects the larger way many of us think of fantasies, even our own.
sentences.zh: 但这同时也反映了我们许多人看待幻想的普遍方式，即使是我们自己的幻想。

sentences.en: We react to their content instead of asking about their origins.
sentences.zh: 我们对它们的内容做出反应，而不是去询问它们的起源。

sentences.en: Rather than seeing them as an imperfect way our minds are responding to trauma,
sentences.zh: 我们没有把它们看作是我们大脑应对创伤的一种不完美方式，

sentences.en: we recoil from them because we fear what they might reveal about our inner demons.
sentences.zh: 反而因为害怕它们可能揭示出我们内心的恶魔而退缩。

sentences.en: When we come back, what would happen if we looked at our fantasies with less judgment
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，如果我们以更少的评判

sentences.en: and more curiosity.
sentences.zh: 和更多的好奇心来看待我们的幻想，会发生什么？

sentences.en: writing it, but it was only writing.

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Once upon a time, there was a boy.
sentences.zh: 从前，有一个小男孩。

sentences.en: One day, he was exploring the mountains near his home
sentences.zh: 有一天，他正在探索家附近的山脉，

sentences.en: when he saw a small white bird fly into a cave.
sentences.zh: 这时他看到一只小白鸟飞进了一个洞穴。

sentences.en: He decided to follow it.
sentences.zh: 他决定跟着它。

sentences.en: At first, it was easy.
sentences.zh: 起初，这很容易。

sentences.en: The bird was bright against the dark rock walls.
sentences.zh: 在黑暗的岩壁衬托下，那只鸟显得很明亮。

sentences.en: But soon, the gloom turned into a suffocating blackness.
sentences.zh: 但很快，阴暗变成了令人窒息的黑暗。

sentences.en: The boy couldn't see the bird anymore.
sentences.zh: 男孩再也看不见那只鸟了。

sentences.en: He couldn't see anything.
sentences.zh: 他什么也看不见。

sentences.en: He wasn't sure how to get back out.
sentences.zh: 他不确定该怎么回去。

sentences.en: He turned in a circle, trying to get his bearings.
sentences.zh: 他转了个圈，试图辨别方向。

sentences.en: And that is when it happened.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，事情发生了。

sentences.en: The sand beneath his feet began to shift and move and open and then...
sentences.zh: 他脚下的沙子开始移动、翻滚、裂开，然后……

sentences.en: Okay, let's stop there.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们停在这里。

sentences.en: You want to know what happens next.
sentences.zh: 你想知道接下来发生了什么。

sentences.en: The truth is, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 事实是，我不知道。

sentences.en: I made up the story to illustrate a point,
sentences.zh: 我编这个故事是为了说明一个观点，

sentences.en: how narratives can take hold of our attention and draw us in.
sentences.zh: 叙事是如何抓住我们的注意力并将我们吸引进去的。

sentences.en: As a lifelong reader, Raymond Marr knows all about the appeal of a good yarn.
sentences.zh: 作为一名终身读者，雷蒙德·马尔非常了解好故事的吸引力。

sentences.en: But as a psychologist at York University in Toronto,
sentences.zh: 但作为多伦多约克大学的一名心理学家，

sentences.en: he's also interested in why stories have the power to hold us captive.
sentences.zh: 他也对为什么故事有能力让我们沉迷其中很感兴趣。

sentences.en: You're in a dreamlike state and you're so deeply immersed within this world
sentences.zh: 你处于一种梦幻般的状态，你深深地沉浸在这个世界里，

sentences.en: that even, you know, if you sort of get jarred out of a piece of fiction
sentences.zh: 以至于，你知道，即使你从一部你非常投入的

sentences.en: that you're highly engaged with,
sentences.zh: 虚构作品中被惊醒，

sentences.en: it kind of takes a while for you to sort of like re-enter the real world.
sentences.zh: 你还是需要一段时间才能重新回到现实世界。

sentences.en: Over the years, Raymond has studied why stories work this way.
sentences.zh: 多年来，雷蒙德研究了为什么故事会以这种方式起作用。

sentences.en: Why are our minds so attuned to narrative and storytelling?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们的大脑如此适应叙事和讲故事？

sentences.en: Think about the last really great book you read.
sentences.zh: 想想你读过的最后一本真正的好书。

sentences.en: If someone asked you what you liked about it,
sentences.zh: 如果有人问你喜欢它什么，

sentences.en: Chances are your answer will be about how the story made you feel.
sentences.zh: 你的回答很可能与这个故事带给你的感受有关。

sentences.en: Raymond says there's a reason for that.
sentences.zh: 雷蒙德说这是有原因的。

sentences.en: This deep sort of immersion in the story, this deep imagination,
sentences.zh: 这种对故事的深度沉浸，这种深度的想象，

sentences.en: draws upon the same sort of emotional systems that we use in the real world.
sentences.zh: 利用了我们在现实世界中使用的相同情感系统。

sentences.en: So the sadness that we feel when a character that we care a lot about dies, for example,
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，当我们关心的角色死亡时，我们感到的悲伤，

sentences.en: it's not the same as a real loved one dying.
sentences.zh: 这与真正的亲人去世是不一样的。

sentences.en: But it's similar enough that it can produce things like tears
sentences.zh: 但它足够相似，以至于可以产生像眼泪

sentences.en: and the same sort of physiological symptoms of sadness.
sentences.zh: 和同样的悲伤生理症状。

sentences.en: And we experience this as sadness.
sentences.zh: 我们将其体验为悲伤。

sentences.en: Some years ago, Raymond analyzed data from studies
sentences.zh: 几年前，雷蒙德分析了研究数据，

sentences.en: in which people were asked to read stories while undergoing brain scans.
sentences.zh: 在这些研究中，人们被要求在进行脑部扫描时阅读故事。

sentences.en: He found that when we are immersed in a story,
sentences.zh: 他发现，当我们沉浸在故事中时，

sentences.en: our brains respond as if we are part of the fictional world
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑反应就好像我们是我们在书页上看到的

sentences.en: that we are seeing on the page.
sentences.zh: 虚构世界的一部分。

sentences.en: So if you have someone read a very simple sentence about a person kicking a soccer ball,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你让某人读一个关于一个人踢足球的非常简单的句子，

sentences.en: not only will you see parts of the language network become involved,
sentences.zh: 你不仅会看到语言网络的部分参与进来，

sentences.en: but you also see activation in the motor cortex,
sentences.zh: 而且你还会看到运动皮层的激活，

sentences.en: the same part of the brain that we use to actually move our bodies.
sentences.zh: 这是我们实际移动身体时使用的大脑同一部分。

sentences.en: And more importantly, this activation is quite specific.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，这种激活是非常具体的。

sentences.en: So you'll only see a part of the motor cortex activated that's related to the lower half of the body.
sentences.zh: 所以你只会看到运动皮层中与身体下半部分相关的部分被激活。

sentences.en: It's worth pausing a moment and underlining this point.
sentences.zh: 值得花点时间停下来，强调一下这一点。

sentences.en: When we read about someone kicking a soccer ball, our brain is activated in the same way as if we were actually the ones kicking the soccer ball.
sentences.zh: 当我们读到有人踢足球时，我们大脑的激活方式，与我们亲身踢球时是一样的。

sentences.en: Raymond began to wonder if something similar happens as our minds process the social challenges that characters encounter in stories.
sentences.zh: 雷蒙德开始思考，当我们的思维处理故事中角色所面临的社会挑战时，是否也会发生类似的情况。

sentences.en: So reading, I believe, it's possible that it presents to us an imagined social world for us to interact with.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，阅读可能会为我们呈现一个想象中的社会世界，让我们与之互动。

sentences.en: So it gives to us a representation of human interactions, human psychology that we can then learn from in very safe circumstances.
sentences.zh: 它为我们提供了一个关于人际互动和人类心理的模拟，让我们能在非常安全的环境中学习。

sentences.en: Put another way, stories give us a chance to experience the real world without the risks of the real world.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，故事让我们有机会在没有现实风险的情况下体验现实世界。

sentences.en: They allow us to run different scenarios and to think about the consequences of those scenarios.
sentences.zh: 它们允许我们模拟不同的情境，并思考这些情境带来的后果。

sentences.en: If we're evaluating a move to a different city, for example,
sentences.zh: 例如，如果我们正在评估是否要搬到另一个城市，

sentences.en: we might imagine what it would be like to live in that city.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会想象住在那个城市会是什么样子。

sentences.en: What would be great about it?
sentences.zh: 那里会有什么好的一面？

sentences.en: What would be awful?
sentences.zh: 又会有什么糟糕的一面？

sentences.en: Stories, daydreams, and fantasies, in other words,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，故事、白日梦和幻想，

sentences.en: allow us to imagine different versions of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 让我们能够想象不同版本的自己。

sentences.en: They allow us to ask,
sentences.zh: 它们让我们能够自问：

sentences.en: what would I do in this situation?
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下我会怎么做？

sentences.en: How would I react?
sentences.zh: 我会如何反应？

sentences.en: What kind of a person would I be?
sentences.zh: 我会成为什么样的人？

sentences.en: Raymond figured that if all of this was true,
sentences.zh: 雷蒙德认为，如果这一切都是真的，

sentences.en: reading about other characters should make us more insightful people.
sentences.zh: 阅读关于其他角色的故事应该会让我们变得更有洞察力。

sentences.en: I had senior colleagues tell me that, you know, you're going to find the exact opposite.
sentences.zh: 我曾有资深同事告诉我，你知道，你可能会发现完全相反的结果。

sentences.en: It's people who read a lot that are going to be more socially awkward.
sentences.zh: 读很多书的人反而会在社交上更笨拙。

sentences.en: They're going to have more difficulty in understanding other people.
sentences.zh: 他们在理解他人方面会有更多困难。

sentences.en: Raymond came up with a study.
sentences.zh: 雷蒙德设计了一项研究。

sentences.en: He tallied the reading habits of volunteers and then had them take a teSt.
sentences.zh: 他统计了志愿者的阅读习惯，然后让他们参加了一项测试。

sentences.en: It's called the reading the mind in the eyes teSt.
sentences.zh: 这被称为“通过眼睛读心”测试。

sentences.en: Volunteers were asked to examine the photographs of people's faces.
sentences.zh: 志愿者被要求观察人们面部的照片。

sentences.en: Specifically, the photos showed only people's eyes.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，照片只显示了人们的眼睛。

sentences.en: Could volunteers tell what emotion the person in the photo was experiencing
sentences.zh: 志愿者能否仅凭眼神中的表情，

sentences.en: using only the expression in their eyes?
sentences.zh: 判断出照片中的人正在经历什么情绪？

sentences.en: And what we found was that people who were exposed to more narrative fiction
sentences.zh: 我们的发现是，接触更多叙事性小说的人，

sentences.en: did better on this test of understanding what other people are thinking
sentences.zh: 在理解他人想法和感受，以及判断他人心理状态的测试中，

sentences.en: and feeling and what their mental states are.
sentences.zh: 表现得更好。

sentences.en: So there was a positive correlation.
sentences.zh: 所以，这之间存在正相关关系。

sentences.en: Now, a correlation is just an association.
sentences.zh: 不过，相关性仅仅是一种关联。

sentences.en: We don't know that reading books caused people to be better at reading the mental states of other people.
sentences.zh: 我们并不知道是阅读书籍导致人们更擅长解读他人的心理状态。

sentences.en: It's entirely possible that the reverse could be true,
sentences.zh: 完全有可能事实恰恰相反，

sentences.en: that people that are really good at understanding other people are also interested in fiction
sentences.zh: 即那些非常擅长理解他人的人，也对小说感兴趣，

sentences.en: because fiction portrays social content,
sentences.zh: 因为小说描绘了社会内容，

sentences.en: or that some third variable explains the association between these two things.
sentences.zh: 或者有某种第三变量解释了这两者之间的关联。

sentences.en: What is clear, however, is that you cannot follow books and movies
sentences.zh: 然而显而易见的是，如果你不能熟练地判断出各种角色内心在发生什么，

sentences.en: without being able to skillfully tell what's happening in the minds of various characters.
sentences.zh: 你就无法看懂书籍和电影。

sentences.en: Appreciating a story requires you to see the world through the perspectives of other people.
sentences.zh: 欣赏一个故事需要你从他人的视角看世界。

sentences.en: It requires empathy.
sentences.zh: 这需要同理心。

sentences.en: So if John gets into a fight or a conflict with a playmate and then he leaves,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果约翰和玩伴打架或发生冲突后离开了，

sentences.en: you might have to make the inference that he left because he was upset.
sentences.zh: 你可能得推断出他离开是因为他心烦意乱。

sentences.en: Or that he left because he won, or that he left because he lost,
sentences.zh: 或者他离开是因为他赢了，又或者是因为他输了，

sentences.en: or he left because he was humiliated
sentences.zh: 或者他离开是因为他感到羞辱，

sentences.en: or any number of different mental states.

sentences.en: what I really saw, what it was like, you know,
sentences.zh: 我真正看到的，那是什么感觉，你知道，

sentences.en: being a child who kind of had to live with two people
sentences.zh: 作为一个孩子，不得不和两个

sentences.en: so, so obsessed with their own, kind of their own needs, their own wants,
sentences.zh: 如此沉迷于自己的需求、自己的欲望的人生活在一起，

sentences.en: and then throw in that whole drinking and partying.
sentences.zh: 再加上那些酗酒和派对。

sentences.en: So, yeah, so this first book was really allowed me to delve into it
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这本书真的让我深入挖掘了这些，

sentences.en: and kind of get my own say, have a say that I never got to say.
sentences.zh: 并表达了我从未有机会表达的观点。

sentences.en: I think it's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这太迷人了。

sentences.en: You're almost trying to master what happened to you.
sentences.zh: 你几乎是在试图掌控发生在你身上的事。

sentences.en: You're almost processing what happened to you.
sentences.zh: 你几乎是在处理发生在你身上的事。

sentences.en: And by putting it into the lives of characters,
sentences.zh: 通过将它融入角色的生活，

sentences.en: in some ways you're able to, in some ways, do what people do in therapy,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，你能够做到人们在治疗中所做的事，

sentences.en: which is to hold their own experiences at some distance
sentences.zh: 那就是将自己的经历保持一定的距离，

sentences.en: and look at themselves and look at their own lives
sentences.zh: 审视自己，审视自己的生活，

sentences.en: and look at their own experiences with some degree of objectivity
sentences.zh: 并以某种客观的角度审视自己的经历，

sentences.en: and allows you to get new insight into what actually happened to you.
sentences.zh: 这让你对真正发生在你身上的事有了新的洞察。

sentences.en: Is that the way it felt for you, Krista?
sentences.zh: 克里斯塔，你当时的感觉是这样吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And I think it brought, even though what I wrote was harsh
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，尽管我写的东西很刺耳，

sentences.en: or maybe could be conceived as cruel,
sentences.zh: 或者可能被认为是残酷的，

sentences.en: It actually helped me understand these characters more.
sentences.zh: 但它实际上帮助我更深入地理解了这些角色。

sentences.en: She also got to do what Jilly Bolton talked about,
sentences.zh: 她还做到了吉莉·博尔顿所说的那样，

sentences.en: reframe stories and rewrite how they ended.
sentences.zh: 重构故事并改写结局。

sentences.en: So the frat boy who dumped her at the party,
sentences.zh: 所以那个在派对上甩了她的兄弟会男生，

sentences.en: Krista turned him into a loser.
sentences.zh: 克里斯塔把他写成了一个失败者。

sentences.en: I mean, we had to really stick the knife in
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们真的得狠狠地补上一刀，

sentences.en: and then give it a nice little turn.
sentences.zh: 然后再转上一圈。

sentences.en: We leave him as just some douchebag in a bar.
sentences.zh: 我们让他以酒吧里一个人渣的形象收场。

sentences.en: You know, that's where we leave him.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是我们让他留下的结局。

sentences.en: The teacher whose constant snapping drove Krista away from music,
sentences.zh: 那个总是挑剔、让克里斯塔远离音乐的老师，

sentences.en: she became Mindy Lancaster,
sentences.zh: 她变成了明迪·兰开斯特，

sentences.en: a dour woman constantly trying to belittle the heroine.
sentences.zh: 一个总是试图贬低女主角的刻薄女人。

sentences.en: In Krista's new version, it was the heroine, Emma, who got the last word.
sentences.zh: 在克里斯塔的新版本中，是女主角艾玛说了最后的话。

sentences.en: What if she couldn't do it?
sentences.zh: 如果她做不到怎么办？

sentences.en: What if her fingers had forgotten?
sentences.zh: 如果她的手指忘记了呢？

sentences.en: What was one second nature?
sentences.zh: 那些曾经是第二天性的东西？

sentences.en: She met Mindy's gaze and saw a glimmer of triumph flash in the woman's eyes.
sentences.zh: 她迎上明迪的目光，看到那个女人眼中闪过一丝胜利的微光。

sentences.en: Mindy was an accomplished pianist,
sentences.zh: 明迪是一位有成就的钢琴家，

sentences.en: but she'd never risen to even a fraction of what Em had achieved as a musician.
sentences.zh: 但她取得的成就连艾姆的一小部分都比不上。

sentences.en: A confidence Em hadn't known in years surged through her veins.
sentences.zh: 一种艾姆多年未曾有过的自信涌上心头。

sentences.en: I'll do fine without the sheet music, Mrs. Lancaster.
sentences.zh: 没有乐谱我也能弹得很好，兰开斯特夫人。

sentences.en: I guess you don't remember, but I mastered these pieces by my fourth birthday.
sentences.zh: 我想你不记得了，但我四岁时就掌握了这些曲子。

sentences.en: Maybe it was my fifth, but who's counting?
sentences.zh: 也许是五岁，但谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: The anger that kept her away from music,
sentences.zh: 那股让她远离音乐的愤怒，

sentences.en: away from the memories that threatened to tear her apart with guilt and grief,
sentences.zh: 远离那些威胁要用内疚和悲伤将她撕碎的记忆，

sentences.en: was transforming.
sentences.zh: 正在发生转变。

sentences.en: I've performed for the Queen of England.
sentences.zh: 我曾为英国女王表演过。

sentences.en: I think I can handle this.
sentences.zh: 我想我能应付这个。

sentences.en: Writing Mindy Lancaster, Krista says, was deeply healing.
sentences.zh: 克里斯塔说，写明迪·兰开斯特的过程非常治愈。

sentences.en: It was surprisingly cathartic.
sentences.zh: 这出奇地具有宣泄作用。

sentences.en: You know, I'd never said anything as a child.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我小时候什么都没说。

sentences.en: I just stopped playing.
sentences.zh: 我只是停止了弹琴。

sentences.en: I just, I never got the chance to say to this woman, you know,
sentences.zh: 我只是，我从来没有机会对这个女人说，你知道，

sentences.en: you took something very important away from me, and I'm angry about it.
sentences.zh: 你夺走了我非常重要的东西，我对此感到愤怒。

sentences.en: After she put all her grief and rage into the fantasy,
sentences.zh: 在她将所有的悲伤和愤怒投入到虚构故事中之后，

sentences.en: Krista says something amazing happened.
sentences.zh: 克里斯塔说发生了一件了不起的事。

sentences.en: I have exposed every raw feeling that I had about that situation,
sentences.zh: 我把对那件事的所有真实感受都倾诉了出来，

sentences.en: and that brings me sort of a peacefulness that it's out there.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到一种平静，因为一切都已释怀。

sentences.en: It almost cleared the way to remember that there were happier memories.
sentences.zh: 它几乎为我扫清了障碍，让我记起其实还有更快乐的回忆。

sentences.en: It just gave me the happiness that was taken away.
sentences.zh: 它找回了我曾经失去的快乐。

sentences.en: I mean, there's also the fact that it's brought you success.
sentences.zh: 我是说，还有个事实是，这为你带来了成功。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, so, you know, you've actually taken this pain and you've transmuted it almost literally into gold.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你看，你实际上把这些痛苦几乎是字面意义上地转化成了黄金。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's become my career.
sentences.zh: 它成了我的事业。

sentences.en: My husband's like, how many jerks did you date?
sentences.zh: 我丈夫问我，你到底约会过多少混蛋？

sentences.en: Because we need some more books.
sentences.zh: 因为我们需要更多的素材来写书。

sentences.en: I tell people I dated every jerk in Denver before I met my husband.
sentences.zh: 我告诉人们，在遇到我丈夫之前，我约会过丹佛所有的混蛋。

sentences.en: So I'm like, honey, you don't have to worry.
sentences.zh: 所以我对他说，亲爱的，你不用担心。

sentences.en: Between college and dating, we're golden.
sentences.zh: 从大学到约会经历，我们的素材绰绰有余。

sentences.en: So, it is just really interesting to take all the heartache and kind of spin it into gold.
sentences.zh: 所以，把所有的心碎转化成黄金，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: With each new book, Krista Sandor has felt like the burdens she has carried have grown lighter and lighter.
sentences.zh: 随着每一本新书的问世，克里斯塔·桑多尔感到她肩上的负担越来越轻。

sentences.en: The themes of anger and sadness have given way to laughter and comedy.
sentences.zh: 愤怒和悲伤的主题已经让位于欢笑和喜剧。

sentences.en: Writing for her has been like a cleansing rain, washing away bad memories and hurt.
sentences.zh: 写作对她来说就像一场涤荡心灵的雨，洗去了痛苦的记忆和伤害。

sentences.en: It has put her in touch with all the good things in her life.
sentences.zh: 它让她重新感受到了生活中所有美好的事物。

sentences.en: Many of us never think to put pen to paper.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人从没想过要动笔写作。

sentences.en: Or we sit down and start, but then hesitate,
sentences.zh: 或者我们坐下来开始写，但又犹豫不决，

sentences.en: because we're afraid of what our stories mean,
sentences.zh: 因为我们害怕自己的故事意味着什么，

sentences.en: what our fantasies might reveal.
sentences.zh: 害怕我们的幻想可能会揭示什么。

sentences.en: But when we do this,
sentences.zh: 但当我们这样做的时候，

sentences.en: we not only miss out on how our stories might transform other people,
sentences.zh: 我们不仅错过了我们的故事如何改变他人的机会，

sentences.en: we miss out on the power of stories to transform us.
sentences.zh: 也错过了故事本身改变我们自己的力量。

sentences.zh: 也是《有用的错觉》的核心主题。

sentences.zh: 几年来，马特一直帮助我和我的合著者比尔·梅斯勒

sentences.zh: 完善我们的想法。

sentences.zh: 但比起他作为编辑的专业能力，

sentences.en: Matt has always been kind and wise,
sentences.zh: 马特一直都很善良且睿智，

sentences.zh: 他是最好的朋友，

sentences.zh: 我能看到他的影响

sentences.zh: 谢谢你，马特。

sentences.zh: 来为原本混乱的世界带来秩序。
